source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Choose transport or energy-use actions that reduce fossil-fuel use and explain why they help.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Halving daily petrol use halves the time before petrol runs out.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: Reduce solar-energy use so that sunlight does not run out.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: Always choose the smallest vehicle; it uses the least fossil fuel per traveller.

mx.name: mechanism_conflation
mx.teacher_note: Choose CNG: cleaner exhaust means less fossil fuel is used.

intelligence.enrichment: Fossil fuels are found in limited quantities. If people continue using them in the current manner, they will run out, so alternate sources and actions such as walking, cycling, and using public transport help conserve fossil fuels. Reducing petrol, diesel, natural gas, or coal use lowers the rate at which limited fossil fuels are consumed, delaying exhaustion and encouraging alternate sources. The learner correctly applies this rule: Fossil fuels are found in limited quantities. If people continue using them in the current manner, they will run out, so alternate sources and actions such as walking, cycling, and using public transport help conserve fossil fuels. Cleaner or convenient fuel choices automatically conserve fossil fuels no matter how much is used.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 6 Science question. Chapter: Nature's treasures. The student must decide: Choose transport or energy-use actions that reduce fossil-fuel use and explain why they help. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key. Do not print mix-up labels, hinge codes, node codes, or the word CANDIDATE. Recalculate the key; do not copy source.key. Every option must be a claim that could answer the stem, and wrong options must be the same kind of answer as the key (a next term, a named process, or a row of the same shape). If the stem continues a number list, every option names a next term. Never write that naming or writing a term is what creates the list. If the stem numbers activities 1..n, every number must appear in an option (or in a structured part's first-class options). Two-tier (choose, then reason) is welcome: put A/B/C on p
